title: Opportunistic infections
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's infection (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for CMV disease.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is an 89-year-old female presenting with persistent fever and elevated liver enzymes. Laboratory workup was significant for cytomegalovirus infection. Patient was started on valganciclovir and instructed to monitor for symptomatic changes. 
[Update] Patient returns today for follow-up while continuing current treatment. She reports that her fever has decreased in frequency but she continues to experience mild fatigue. She denies new rashes or significant abdominal pain.

Vitals: BP 128/74, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.4F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for mild fatigue. Negative for chills, night sweats.
HEENT: Negative for sore throat, rhinorrhea.
Respiratory: Negative for cough, shortness of breath.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.
Skin: Negative for new rashes.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears comfortable.
Skin: No visible rashes or lesions.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly.

Assessment:
1. Cytomegalovirus disease: Patient is currently undergoing treatment with valganciclovir. Liver tests remain stable.

Plan:
1. Continue valganciclovir as prescribed.
2. Monitor liver function tests and CBC.
3. Follow up in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
October 14, 2026
explanations: Cytomegalovirus disease, site not specified: B25.9 (HCC 6).
